key_insight: Decomposing humanoid control into intuitive submodules and training a scalable learning layer of "choice policies" enables robust, coordinated whole-body manipulation across head, hands, and legs with teleoperation-friendly interfaces.
problem_solved: Enables reliable whole-body coordination for humanoid robots in human-centric environments by addressing the complexity of simultaneously controlling head, arms/hands, and locomotion.
method: Design a modular teleoperation interface that breaks control into submodules: hand–eye coordination, grasp primitives, arm end-effector tracking, and locomotion.
Train a scalable learning framework of choice policies that selects and coordinates submodules to produce smooth, context-aware whole-body actions.
Integrate teleoperation data and policy learning to allow intuitive human control while enabling autonomous switching and refined behaviors.
impact: Makes whole-body humanoid manipulation more scalable, interpretable, and practical for deployment—reducing operator burden and improving robustness for real-world tasks in robotics and ML research.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: modular teleoperation interface mapped to choice-policy layer and robot actuators (head, arms, legs).
Flowchart: decision-making by choice policies selecting submodules (e.g., grasp vs locomotion) during a manipulation task.
Before/after sequence: side-by-side frames showing uncoordinated vs coordinated whole-body manipulation.
Bar/line chart: performance metrics (success rate, stability, operator workload) comparing baseline vs choice-policy approach.
paper_title: Coordinated Humanoid Manipulation with Choice Policies
paper_authors: Haozhi Qi, Yen-Jen Wang, Toru Lin, Brent Yi, Yi Ma
